The buildout of public fast-charging infrastructure for electric vehicles is accelerating. According to the Department of Transportation's mid-year tally, 3,200 DC fast chargers were in operation nationwide, a 41% increase over the same period last year. Installations were concentrated at highway rest stops and big-box store parking lots, and 38% of the total sits in major metro areas.

Average utilization, however, came in at just 27%, prompting criticism that "placement is out of step with demand." An industry representative said chargers should be redeployed to reflect overnight demand in dense apartment districts and older downtown neighborhoods. The department said it will start factoring utilization data into siting approvals in the second half of the year.
